text:
Sam H: Heads-up — ran an overnight staged-batcher/allocator exercise on the canary fleet. Saw p95 increase ~18% for short-gen sessions (<=32 tokens). Replays attached.

Ria P: :eyes: can you paste profiler/sample metrics + kernel picks?

Sam H: quick dump from the run:
```
kernel=matmul_v3
avg_batch_size=9 -> 12
allocator=staged-batcher
kv_hits=0.72
p50=14ms p95=210ms (+18%)
helix_switches=~1200/min
```
Seems like decode path is experiencing more kernel handoffs and handshake waits.

Kenji M: From the flamegraphs i pulled, prefill stage looks steady. Decode shows a lot of micro-batch churn: 12-token coalesces -> split into 4-token kernels repeatedly. That thrash triggers fallback kernel selection and increases latency. Token-budget target for decode is probably too generous for the small sessions.

Taylor G: Suggestion: reduce decode token_budget target to ~8 for short sessions, and widen prefill burst window so prefill can coalesce. Also try setting kernel_affinity for small batches (force matmul_small_opt) to avoid repeated kernel lookups. Low-risk A/B.

Ria P: Did the overnight run have KV priming enabled? If priming was off, handshake times will be worse.

Sam H: I intentionally disabled KV priming to isolate batching behavior. I did a small follow-up with priming on and saw p95 improve ~6% (to ~197ms) but overall throughput dipped ~1.8%. So priming helps latency spikes but trades a bit of steady throughput.

Kenji M: Config snippet I used for the local experiment:
```
batcher:
  staged_allocator: true
  per_stage_budget:
    prefill: 12
    decode: 8
  kernel_affinity:
    small_batch: matmul_small_opt
    large_batch: matmul_v3
  kv_priming: true
  handshake_timeout_ms: 12
```
Dropping handshake timeout a touch also reduced tail.

Taylor G: Another idea: fallback policy based on kv_hit ratio. If kv_hits < 0.6 and p95 > 200ms, route decode to a larger-kernel fallback (less frequent kernel switches). That should smooth transient spikes while we tune budgets.

Sam H: ran experiment-357 with that fallback rule enabled. Quick numbers: p95 -> 185ms, p99 unchanged; request throughput basically flat. I uploaded the logs and kernel-switch histogram here: https://gist.redwood/example-experiment-357

deploy-bot: deploy started for experiment-357 by @Sam H :rocket:

Ria P: :thumbsup: Nice. Action items: 1) Run 24h canary skewed to short-gen traffic with staged allocator + decode budget=8 + kv_priming=true + fallback rule. 2) Add telemetry for kernel_switch_count, handshake_waits, kv_hit_latency buckets. 3) Collect result + perf regression checks.

Kenji M: I'll add counters for handshake_waits and batch_coalesces, and emit a metric for kernel_affinity_hits.

Sam H: Thanks — scheduling the canary now. Will post the morning summary with graphs.

Taylor G: If canary looks good we'll roll the decode budget change as a temporary mitigation and follow up with a more aggressive kernel-selection policy (quieter switching algorithm).

Sam H: Sounds good. Thanks all. :coffee:
